Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

These are selections on the air job multi-select, not confirmed events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance these are reported as a training item: technicians should select stop-work authority only when it was actually used, and may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe. Two things stand out today. First, "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on a single form — every stop-work selection today was the routine "discussed" item. Second, the identical observe string recurs across technicians and jobs, which points to a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh each time.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text — so the only way those reached this report is when a technician typed them into a comments field, as Dawson Drake did. The same applies to anything wrong with a trailer that a photo would show but no field records.

One further limitation specific to tonight: this review ran at 11:00 PM Central on the day being reviewed, so the usual second pass over the following morning's mail could not be run. Submissions for 10/15 that arrive overnight or tomorrow morning are not included here. Three submissions received today carry form dates from previous days and were read but are not counted toward 10/15 coverage: Jerry Gonzales 35783 and Joseph Popillion 35641 and 35637, all dated 10/14.
